mainTopic: Turning a loan into a debt of produce: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא, the dispute between רב and רבי ינאי, and רבי יהודה's view on a deal that might become interest.
overview: רבא finishes explaining why he reads the משנה like רבי אושעיא. In רבי אושעיא's ברייתא, a lender keeps switching what he is owed, from money to wheat, then to wine, then to oil, each time at today's price. This is allowed only if the borrower actually has the produce. רבא reads 'לקח' in the משנה as 'took it as payment for his loan.' He then draws three lessons: a loan may be set up to be paid in produce, only if the borrower has that produce, and the הלכה follows רבי ינאי, who holds that taking the produce or its value makes no difference. The גמרא challenges רב, who disagrees with רבי ינאי, from the same ברייתא. רב הונא answers that the produce was already set aside for the lender in a corner. שמואל answers instead that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who permits a deal that only might become interest, and the גמרא proves this from a ברייתא about a field 'sold' to a lender. אביי and רבא give two different explanations of that dispute, and רבא begins a new point based on רבי ינאי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's reason: רבי אושעיא fits the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his statement: he follows רבי אושעיא because the משנה can be explained according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because I can explain the משנה according to his view.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רבא's sentence from just before. רבא says he prefers רבי אושעיא's approach because it lets him explain the משנה smoothly. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא was using a different ברייתא (from רבי חייא) to understand the משנה. רבא wants to explain the משנה through רבי אושעיא instead. His reason is simple: the משנה lines up with רבי אושעיא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: for I explain our Mishnah according to him.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבא's sentence from just before; 'him' is רבי אושעיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement begun before this section, giving his reason for preferring רבי אושעיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is best explained according to רבי אושעיא's ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's case: money turns into wheat, wheat into wine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: a lender asks for his money to buy wheat, and the borrower gives wheat at today's price. Later the lender asks for the wheat to buy wine, and the borrower offers wine at today's price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא taught: Someone was owed a מנה by his friend. He went and stood by the friend's threshing floor and said, 'Give me my money, because I want to buy wheat with it.' The borrower said, 'I have wheat to give you. Go figure out how much I owe you at today's price.' When the time came to sell wheat, the lender said, 'Give me the wheat, because I want to sell it and buy wine.' The borrower said, 'I have wine to give you. Go figure it out at today's price.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes the ברייתא of רבי אושעיא. It tells the story of a debt that keeps changing form, first from money into wheat and then from wheat into wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time, the debt is turned into a set amount of produce at the price on that day. The produce stays with the borrower. So the lender's claim is now for produce, not for money. That is why the question of רבית (interest) comes up if the price later goes up.

keyTerms.meaning: is owed by / is a creditor of
threshing floor, where the grain is
set it up as owed by me

phrases.english: As Rabbi Oshaya teaches:
One who was owed a maneh by his friend,
and he went and stood by his threshing floor
and said: Give me my money,
because I want to buy wheat with it.
And he said to him: I have wheat
that I will give you;

phrases.aramaic: צֵא וַעֲשָׂאֵן עָלַי כְּשַׁעַר שֶׁל עַכְשָׁיו.
phrases.english: go and set it up as owed by me at the current price.
phrases.notes: He means: work out how much wheat my debt equals at today's price, and I'll owe you that much wheat.

phrases.english: When the time to sell wheat arrived,
he said to him: Give me wheat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְמוֹכְרָן וְלִיקַּח בָּהֶן יַיִן.
phrases.english: because I want to sell it and buy wine with it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: יֵשׁ לִי יַיִן שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have wine that I will give you;

phrases.aramaic: צֵא וַעֲשָׂאֵן עָלַי כְּשַׁעַר שֶׁל עַכְשָׁיו.
phrases.english: go and set it up as owed by me at the current price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that step 1 said fits the משנה.

steps.title: Wine turns into oil, and the rule: only if he has it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with wine turning into oil. Then it rules: in all these cases it is permitted if the borrower has the produce, and forbidden if he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the time came to sell wine, the lender said, 'Give me my wine, because I want to sell it and buy oil.' The borrower said, 'I have oil to give you. Go figure it out at today's price.' In all these cases, if he has it, it is permitted. If he does not have it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more switch, from wine to oil. Then it gives its ruling for every case: it depends on whether the borrower actually has the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower really owns the produce, it is as if he paid the lender in produce right now. Any later rise in price belongs to the lender as an owner. If the borrower does not have it, the lender may end up collecting more than his loan just because he waited. That is רבית, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: if he has it (the produce on hand)

steps.whatToRemember: Turning a debt into produce at today's price is allowed only when the borrower really has that produce.

phrases.english: When the time to sell wine arrived,
he said to him: Give me my wine

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי רוֹצֶה לְמוֹכְרוֹ וְלִיקַּח בּוֹ שֶׁמֶן.
phrases.english: because I want to sell it and buy oil with it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמֶן יֵשׁ לִי שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have oil that I will give you;

phrases.aramaic: צֵא וַעֲשֵׂהוּ עָלַי כְּשַׁעַר שֶׁל עַכְשָׁיו.
phrases.english: go and set it up as owed by me at the current price.
In all of them, if he has it, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: 'Has it' means the borrower actually owns the wheat, wine or oil he is promising.

phrases.english: If he does not have it, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's story and gives its ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converting a debt into produce at the current price is permitted only if the borrower has the produce.

steps.title: Reading 'he took' in the משנה as payment for a loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'לקח' in the משנה means the lender took the wheat as payment for his loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'he took' mean? He took it as payment for his loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now applies the ברייתא to the משנה. He explains that the word 'לקח' there does not mean an ordinary purchase. It means the lender took the wheat in place of the money he had lent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary purchase is not a loan, so it would be hard to see why the משנה calls it רבית. By reading 'לקח' as 'took it for his loan,' the משנה's case becomes the same as רבי אושעיא's case. That is exactly why רבא said the משנה fits רבי אושעיא.

keyTerms.meaning: he took / acquired (the word used in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'לקח' in the משנה as a normal purchase with cash. רבא says the wheat was taken as payment for an old loan, and that is why רבית is a concern.

phrases.english: And what is 'he took'? He took it as payment for his loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא back to the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לקח' might mean an ordinary purchase of wheat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לקח' means he took the wheat as payment for a loan, just like רבי אושעיא's case.

steps.title: Three lessons from רבי אושעיא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא draws three conclusions: a loan may be set up to be paid in produce; this is allowed only if the borrower has the produce; and the הלכה follows רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn three things from רבי אושעיא. Learn that a loan may be set up to be paid in produce, and we do not say this is like a case where his איסר has not yet reached his hand. Learn that this applies only where he has the produce. And learn that the הלכה follows רבי ינאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sums up what the ברייתא teaches. He lists three הלכות that come out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a loan can be turned into a debt of produce. We do not object that the lender never actually received anything, which is the concern in רבי חייא's ברייתא. Second, this works only if the borrower owns the produce. Third, the ברייתא supports the view of רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it / conclude from it
one may set up a loan to be paid in produce
his איסר (coin) that came into his hand

steps.whatToRemember: From רבי אושעיא: (1) a loan may be set up to be paid in produce; (2) only if the borrower has the produce; (3) the הלכה follows רבי ינאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for turning debts into produce without breaking the איסור of רבית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא תְּלָת.
phrases.english: Rava said: Learn from Rabbi Oshaya's teaching three things.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּמַעֲמִידִין מִלְוֶה עַל גַּבֵּי פֵּירוֹת,
phrases.english: Learn from it that one may set up a loan upon produce,
phrases.notes: He means the borrower may now owe a set amount of produce, figured at today's price, instead of money.

phrases.english: and we do not say
that it is not like his issar that came into his hand.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי חייא's ברייתא: the lender never actually got anything into his hand, so it isn't a real purchase.

phrases.english: And learn from it: only where he has it.
And learn from it: the view of Rabbi Yannai stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical halachos out of the ברייתא that was just used to explain the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A loan may be turned into a produce debt at the current price only if the borrower has the produce, and the הלכה follows רבי ינאי.

steps.title: What רבי ינאי holds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the view of רבי ינאי: produce or its value, it makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ינאי said: What difference is it to me whether it is the produce itself or its value?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא just said the הלכה follows רבי ינאי, and now the גמרא tells us what רבי ינאי actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ינאי, once the loan is set up as a debt of produce, the lender may take either the produce or its money value. Taking the value is not seen as interest, because it is worth exactly the same as the produce he is owed.

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי הֵן מָה לִי דְּמֵיהֶן
keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make: the produce itself or its value

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yannai said:
What difference is it to me if it is them (the produce)
what difference is it to me if it is their value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבי ינאי whom רבא ruled like in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the money value of the produce owed is the same as taking the produce itself.

steps.title: The full disagreement between רב and רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: רב allows a loan arranged for produce but not for its money value; רבי ינאי sees no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: רב says, one may make a trust arrangement for produce, but one may not make a trust arrangement for money. And רבי ינאי says: What difference is it to me whether it is the produce or its value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the original מחלוקת so we can see who argues with רבי ינאי. This sets up the objection against רב that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the lender may be paid back in produce. They argue about whether he may then take the produce's money value instead. רב forbids it because it looks like getting back more money than he lent, while רבי ינאי sees it as the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a trust arrangement: giving money now to be paid back later

steps.confusionAlert: רב does not forbid paying back in produce. He only forbids switching to the money value of the produce.

phrases.english: As it was stated: Rav says:
One may make a trust arrangement with produce.
phrases.notes: He means you may lend money now and agree to be paid back later in produce.

phrases.english: But one may not make a trust arrangement with money (value).
And Rabbi Yannai says:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי הֵן, וּמָה לִי דְּמֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: What difference is it to me if it is the produce, and what difference if it is their value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full מחלוקת behind רבי ינאי's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: produce yes, its money value no. רבי ינאי: both are allowed.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to argue against רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows all the switches if the borrower has the produce, which seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: In all of them, if he has the produce, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using the ברייתא from earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the lender did not take the wheat itself. He switched it to wine at its value, and later to oil. That is like taking the value of the produce, which רב forbids, yet the ברייתא allows it when the borrower has the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them: all the cases listed

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
In all of them, if he has (the produce), it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's side of the מחלוקת just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that one may not take the money value of produce owed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the lender switch his produce debt to its value in another item, which is taking value, and calls it permitted.

steps.title: The lender actually acquired the produce
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב says the ברייתא speaks of a lender who pulled the produce and acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: It is talking about where he pulled it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's side answers the objection by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender did משיכה on the wheat, it already belongs to him. Switching it to wine is just selling his own wheat, not taking value for a loan, so רב has no problem with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulled: משיכה, a way of acquiring movable items

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Where he pulled (the produce).
phrases.notes: The lender pulled the wheat toward himself, which makes it his.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא speaks of produce still owed, which would be taking value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of produce the lender already acquired.

steps.title: That would be too obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he pulled the produce, why would the ברייתא need to say it is allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pulled it, does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender truly owns the wheat, of course he may trade it for wine. A ברייתא would not bother to teach something so plain, so this answer seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it need to be said? (meaning it is obvious)

phrases.english: If it is where he pulled,
does it need to be said?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's explanation that the lender pulled the produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lender fully acquired it, the ruling is obvious and the ברייתא would not need to teach it.

steps.title: The borrower set aside a corner for the lender
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of a borrower who set aside a corner with the produce for the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he set aside a corner for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer with a case that is less obvious than pulling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting aside a corner is not a full act of acquiring, so it is not obvious. Still, the ברייתא teaches that for this הלכה it is enough, so the produce counts as the lender's, and switching it is not taking value of a loan.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the ברייתא is only allowing the switch because the produce was already set aside for the lender.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case
where he set aside a corner for him.
phrases.notes: The borrower marked off a corner where the lender's produce sits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן שֶׁיִּחֵד לוֹ קֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא speaks of a lender who pulled the produce, which is too obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a corner set aside for him, which is a new teaching.

steps.title: שמואל: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers differently: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who permits a deal that only might involve interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who said: a case that might go either way regarding interest is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, different answer to the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of changing the case, שמואל says the ברייתא follows one תנא. רבי יהודה allows a deal where, at the start, it is not sure there will be interest at all. So the ברייתא is not a proof for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A deal that may or may not end up as interest

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said:
One side of interest is permitted.
phrases.notes: Literally 'one side'. He means the deal could end up as interest or not, and nobody knows yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the objection of step 8, instead of רב הונא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to one particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a general rule that goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who permits a deal that might or might not be interest.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a field sold to the lender in place of a debt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's view: when a borrower 'sells' his field to the lender, the seller may eat the produce. The buyer may not, but רבי יהודה permits even the buyer to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: A person was owed a מנה (100 dinars) by his friend, and the friend sold him his field. If the seller eats the produce, it is allowed. If the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden. רבי יהודה says: even if the buyer eats the produce, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה permits a deal that only might turn into interest. The source is a ברייתא about a borrower who 'sells' his field to the lender to cover the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale is not final. If the borrower later repays the מנה, the field goes back to him. If the lender ate the produce in the meantime, it turns out he received extra value just for waiting for his money, and that is interest. The חכמים therefore forbid the buyer to eat the produce, while רבי יהודה permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
The seller, which here is the borrower
The buyer, which here is the lender

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up about who is who. The 'seller' (מוכר) is the borrower, and the 'buyer' (לוקח) is the lender who is owed the money.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה נוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה,
phrases.english: As it is taught: If one was owed a hundred dinars by his friend,
and the friend made his field into a sale for him.
phrases.notes: The borrower 'sells' the field to cover the debt, but if he pays the money back, he gets the field back.

phrases.english: When the seller eats the produce, it is permitted.
If the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden.
רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַלּוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Even when the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for שמואל's statement that רבי יהודה permits a deal that only might involve interest.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה permits צד אחד ברבית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יהודה permits even the buyer (the lender) to eat the produce.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story about ביתוס בן זונין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a real case. ביתוס בן זונין made such a sale on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer ate the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to them: There was a case with ביתוס בן זונין, who sold his field this way on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer was the one eating the produce!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה backs up his lenient view with a story. A great sage approved this kind of deal even though the buyer ate the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof from an actual event (a מעשה). If רבי אלעזר בן עזריה approved a deal in which the lender ate the produce, then it must be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A real event or case, brought as a proof

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the חכמים, the first opinion in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: There was an incident with ביתוס בן זונין
who made his field into a sale

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
and the buyer was the one eating the produce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה supports the lenient view he gave in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the buyer may eat the produce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of ביתוס בן זונין, which was approved by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the story
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the story is no proof, because in that case it was the seller who ate the produce, not the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? It was the seller who ate the produce, not the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's story. They say the facts were different from how he told them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not argue with the logic of the proof. They argue with the facts. If the seller ate the produce, the case fits everyone's view, so it proves nothing about a buyer eating the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (said to reject a proof)

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there a proof from there?!

phrases.aramaic: מוֹכֵר אוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹת הָיָה, וְלֹא לוֹקֵחַ.
phrases.english: It was the seller who ate the produce, and not the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's proof from the story in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story. Each side keeps its own view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The facts of the story were told wrongly: the seller ate the produce, not the buyer.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא: the seller may eat the produce. The חכמים forbid the buyer to eat it, and רבי יהודה permits it. The story about ביתוס is disputed, so it settles nothing.

steps.title: What is the real disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the underlying difference is between the חכמים and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the argument is really about. This sets up the two answers that come next, from אביי and from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know what each side rules, but not why. The גמרא wants the reasoning that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that the חכמים and רבי יהודה disagree about.

steps.title: אביי: they argue about a deal that might become interest
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the argument is about צד אחד ברבית, a deal that may or may not turn out to be interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The difference between them is about a deal with one possible side of interest.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. In his view, רבי יהודה permits a deal that only might end up as interest, and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower never repays, the sale becomes final, and the produce was simply the buyer's own. Only if he repays does the produce turn out to be interest. רבי יהודה permits the deal because it is not certain to become interest, and the חכמים forbid it because it might. This matches שמואל's claim in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: A deal that only might turn out to be interest

phrases.english: אביי said:
Uncertain interest is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether a deal that only might become interest is permitted. רבי יהודה permits it.

steps.title: רבא: they argue about interest that will be paid back
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the argument is about רבית על מנת להחזיר, interest taken on the condition that it will be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is about interest taken on the condition that it will be given back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the argument. In his view, the lender eats the produce but must pay for it if the loan is repaid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, רבי יהודה permits the buyer to eat only because he agrees to pay back the value of the produce if the borrower repays the debt. The חכמים forbid even this, since taking interest is still forbidden even when one plans to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest taken on the condition that it will be paid back

phrases.english: רבא said:
Interest on condition to give it back
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: רִבִּית עַל מְנָת לְהַחֲזִיר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 16 than אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether interest taken on the condition that it will be returned is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the dispute is about a deal that might become interest. רבא says it is about interest that will be paid back.

steps.title: רבא begins a new point based on רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new statement, building on something רבי ינאי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that רבי ינאי has said...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא is starting a new point that builds on a teaching of רבי ינאי, and the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'now that' tell us רבא will draw a conclusion from רבי ינאי's teaching. That conclusion comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: רבא said: Now that רבי ינאי says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement by רבא that builds on רבי ינאי's ruling from steps 6–7 (מה לי הן מה לי דמיהן). It continues on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. רבא is about to build on רבי ינאי's teaching.
